prize_parts.citation: For developing small molecules that harness the ubiquitin-proteasome system to induce targeted protein degradation, through heterobifunctional degraders and the cereblon mechanism of molecular glues

statement.case_for: I have moved from B002 to B010. After round 1 no one else ranks B002 first or as an alternative, and I have a field overlap there with Yu and Tsapatsis, so I withdraw it as my preferred part rather than ask colleagues to resolve recusal. On the science, B010 meets my own tests better than I judged in round 1. The principle is general: a small molecule induces a ternary complex between an E3 ligase and a target, and ubiquitin transfer and degradation follow catalytically. It has been reproduced by many independent groups. The structural evidence is real, not inferred: Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target was followed by crystal structures of cereblon-glue-substrate complexes, and ternary-complex structures for VHL-based PROTACs, which show what the molecules do. The glue strand has already produced approved medicines, which answers the maturity concern. B010 has the widest support on the table (two firsts, four top-three rankings, and an alternative for five other members), so it is the one configuration that can plausibly reach five without anyone abandoning scientific judgment. A Crews, Deshaies and Handa trio with a citation naming both the induced-proximity concept and the cereblon mechanism is defensible, because both strands share one chemical idea.
statement.case_against: No heterobifunctional PROTAC is yet approved, so the clinical case for that strand rests on trials, and the approved glue medicines were explained retrospectively. Credit is spread across at least eight people, and a trio leaves out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim, who have real claims. Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are the work I find most persuasive on structural grounds, so I am uneasy that Handa, whose contribution is identifying the target, is preferred to him. A single sentence covering PROTACs and glues could be criticised as joining two discoveries, and the citation would need expert-report confirmation of priority.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation turned induced proximity into a design principle, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as the core and degraders in late-stage trials.
responses.response: Daniel, in round 1 I held back because no degrader was approved and the credit list was wide. I still hold both reservations, but I weigh them differently now. Your framing of an event-driven, catalytic design principle is a chemical discovery in its own right, and it does not depend on one drug approval. I have adopted your trio. I ask only that the citation say 'small molecules that harness the ubiquitin-proteasome system', which you proposed, and that the expert report confirm the trial status.

responses.point: PROTACs and molecular glues share one principle of induced ternary complexes, and the third name could be Handa or Ciulli.
responses.response: Andrei, your question about whether one sentence can cover both strands is the key one, and I think it can, because the shared object is the ternary complex. On the third name, I would choose Handa over Ciulli, though not comfortably. Handa identified cereblon and so explained the glue medicines that already exist, which is the maturity argument. Ciulli's structural work is excellent but is more naturally credited as method development on top of the PROTAC concept. If the expert reports show that the structural ternary-complex work was decisive for the field, I would reopen that choice. I support your citation wording that names the cereblon mechanism.

responses.point: B058 is a strong alternative, since the structures are secure but the N2 binding mode and electron-proton delivery are not, and the C-N coupling candidacy has the cleanest attribution.
responses.response: Peter, I agree with your reading of nitrogenase: the Rees and Einsle structures are secure, and a citation limited to the cofactor structure would drop Seefeldt, which makes it a weaker year-2026 candidate than I implied in round 1. I keep it as an alternative, but not as a lead. Since you and I both distrust unsettled mechanism, I note that B010 has structural evidence for how the complexes form, whereas for nitrogenase the key mechanistic step is still unresolved. Your point about the clean B035 attribution is fair and is why I list it as an alternative.

responses.point: C-N coupling (B035) is the clearest case of a new reaction that became routine, and Kosugi's tin-amide work is a precursor; B010 clinical maturity is a question for you.
responses.response: Peter, I accept your argument that C-N coupling is a distinct reaction with a mechanistic basis in oxidative addition and reductive elimination, and I withdraw my round-1 suggestion that it was only an extension of the 2010 prize. Palladium catalysis was honoured for C-C coupling. I still rank it behind B010 because the 2010 precedent will be raised by others, and because B010 opens a new capability and not a better route to a known bond type. You asked whether B010 is mature enough. Approved glue-class medicines and the late-stage trial status are the facts to confirm in the reports, and on those I find the timing acceptable. B035 stays as my alternative.

responses.point: Biomolecular phase separation (B046) is a physical principle for membraneless organization, and the third laureate could be Rosen, Pappu or Mittag.
responses.response: Heiner, I still do not think the cellular claim is firm enough for a citation worded as 'organizes the interior of living cells'. As a structural chemist I am uneasy because the in-cell state is inferred largely from optical and reconstitution experiments, not from structural measurements that distinguish equilibrium demixing from other assemblies. If the committee wanted a narrower citation on the in vitro thermodynamics of multivalent interactions, Rosen is the part I trust most, and I would then rank B046 acceptable. As worded, I cannot support it as first choice, but your acknowledgement of the debate is honest and I do not dispute the generative value.

responses.point: Massively parallel sequencing (B011) is the clearest game-changer, with a two-name Balasubramanian and Klenerman lineage and a conditional willingness to prefer B010.
responses.response: Johan, I still regard the Solexa chemistry as real chemistry and your two-name narrowing as the disciplined choice. My doubt remains whether its fit lies in Chemistry rather than Physiology or Medicine, which is a boundary question and not a flaw in the science. You list B010 as an alternative and note that you would accept it if the committee wants a new chemical modality. That is my position as well, and I am asking whether you would join B010 if the trial status and approved glue medicines are confirmed, since that would reach three and then move toward five.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports confirm the status of approved glue-class medicines and late-stage PROTAC trials, and whether they support the cereblon strand and the PROTAC strand as one citation.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name, and how to treat Sakamoto, Ito, Kim and Gray in the priority record.
Whether the committee can move from five distinct first choices to five votes without compromising on citation or attribution.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure: my own field is electron crystallography of zeolites and porous materials, and I have a possible field overlap with B002 candidates (Yu, Tsapatsis) through the porous-materials community. I no longer prefer B002, so I do not ask the committee to rule on recusal, but I will abstain from any vote on B002. I have no tie to any candidate in B010, B035 or B058. Peter Brzezinski is a Stockholm University colleague; I disclose it for transparency and see no recusal ground.
